pages.title: 3 – C
pages.body:
- **3D printer:** A printer that builds solid objects layer by layer.
- **Absolute reference:** A cell reference that does not change when copied, e.g. $B$2.
- **Actuator:** A robot part that produces movement, such as a motor or gripper.
- **Assistive technology:** Hardware or software that helps persons with disabilities use computers.
- **Authentication:** Proving the identity of a user.
- **Authorisation:** Deciding what an authenticated user may do.
- **Braille embosser:** A printer that punches raised Braille dots.
- **Charms bar:** A Windows 8 bar with Search, Share, Start, Devices and Settings.
- **Controller:** The computer “brain” of a robot that runs its program.

pages.title: D – H
pages.body:
- **Defragmentation:** Rearranging file pieces on a hard disk so each file is stored together.
- **DNS:** Domain Name System: translates domain names into IP addresses.
- **DTP:** Desktop publishing: designing publications combining text and graphics.
- **Encryption:** Converting plaintext into unreadable ciphertext using a key.
- **Fabrication:** Creating fake data and inserting it into a system.
- **Flash memory:** Non-volatile memory with no moving parts.
- **Flowchart:** A diagram of an algorithm using standard symbols.
- **Function (Excel):** A built-in formula such as SUM or AVERAGE.
- **Hologram:** A 3D image made by recording interference patterns of laser light.

pages.title: H – Q
pages.body:
- **Hyperlink:** Clickable text or image that leads to another location.
- **Interception:** Unauthorised access to data.
- **Interruption:** Making data or a system unavailable.
- **IP address:** A unique number identifying a device on a network.
- **Modification:** Unauthorised changing of data.
- **OSI model:** A seven-layer reference model for network communication.
- **Partition:** A section of a disk treated as a separate drive.
- **Protocol:** A set of rules for communication.
- **QR code:** A square, two-dimensional barcode read by cameras.

pages.title: Q – S
pages.body:
- **Qubit:** A quantum bit that can be in superposition of 0 and 1.
- **Relative reference:** A cell reference that changes when a formula is copied.
- **RFID:** Radio Frequency Identification: reading tags by radio waves.
- **Sensor:** A device that detects or measures a physical property.
- **SmartArt:** Ready-made diagrams in Office applications.
- **SSD:** Solid State Drive: flash-based storage replacing hard disks.
- **Strong AI:** Hypothetical AI with general, human-level intelligence.
- **Superposition:** The ability of a qubit to be in a combination of states.
- **Sycamore:** Google’s 54-qubit quantum processor (2019).

pages.title: T – W
pages.body:
- **Thermal printer:** A printer that uses heat on special paper.
- **Weak AI:** AI designed for a narrow, specific task.
- **WWW:** World Wide Web: linked web pages on the Internet.
